statement: The fixed analysis uses openai/codex commit c9b19deb09c1841ce7acc33ddb96276030936a29; the latest stable release observed was rust-v0.149.0 published on 2026-08-20.
In the pinned source, MemoryTool is Stable but default-disabled; after the feature is enabled, generate_memories and use_memories default true while dedicated_tools defaults false.
Automatic Memory work starts from a qualifying primary turn and skips ephemeral or non-root Agent sessions.

Default startup selection processes threads updated within 10 days, idle for at least 6 hours, and claims at most two rollouts per startup; Phase 2 selects at most 256 candidates and uses a 30-day unused window.
Phase 1 filters rollout items, excludes developer and complete AGENTS/skill context fragments, and applies secret redaction before or after model extraction.
Phase 1 limits rollout content to 70 percent of the active model's effective input window, with a 150000-token fallback when model metadata is unavailable.

Phase 1 emits strict JSON containing free-form raw_memory, rollout_summary and optional rollout_slug; raw_memories.md later contains generated raw_memory text rather than the original rollout transcript.
The default OpenAI provider prefers gpt-5.6-luna at low effort for extraction and gpt-5.6-terra at medium effort for consolidation, subject to config/provider overrides.
Candidate outputs, usage metadata and Memory jobs are persisted in a dedicated memories_1.sqlite with stage1_outputs and jobs tables; final reader-facing knowledge is stored as files.
Phase 2 ranks eligible candidates by usage count, last usage or source recency, then materializes the selected set for global consolidation.
Phase 2 runs as an internal MemoryConsolidation Agent with no network, MCP servers, Apps, Plugins, recursive collaboration or Memory reuse under managed sandboxing.
The consolidation validator checks required files, the v1 summary header and symlink absence, but does not independently verify the factual or provenance semantics of generated Markdown.
The local read path injects at most 2500 tokens of memory_summary.md and then uses file list/read/substring search rather than an embedding or ANN index.

Codex local Memory uses one physical root per CODEX_HOME and one global Phase 2 job; project and worktree scope are primarily represented through cwd, Git metadata and generated document organization.
Parsed Memory citations update the usage_count and last_usage of referenced rollout outputs, creating a citation-driven retention feedback loop.

Subagent sessions do not independently start Memory generation, while inter-agent communication retained in a root rollout may enter that root's extraction; Guardian review sessions explicitly disable Memory use.
The pinned defaults leave disable_on_external_context false, so marking Web/MCP/tool-derived threads polluted is an opt-in policy rather than a mandatory Memory invariant.
Explicit remember, update or forget requests can create append-only ad-hoc notes for later consolidation; the full reset clears Memory DB rows first and file roots second.
Because full reset preserves source rollouts and thread memory modes, still-eligible historical threads can be re-extracted by a later startup.
The pinned Phase 2 selector still uses multiple LIMIT/OFFSET pages outside one read transaction, so the concurrent-insert drift reported in issue 26684 is not excluded by the visible query structure.
Bad Memory reports in a sandboxed synthetic study that planted persistent Memory payloads can influence current and future Codex sessions, with outcomes varying across systems and models.
Post-release Memory-path changes between rust-v0.149.0 and c9b19deb are narrow metadata and extension-prompt changes rather than a replacement of the two-stage architecture.
